Im Hochmittelalter wurde die Beizjagd in: In the High Middle Ages hawking in Europe became an art of the nobility. Around 1240 Emperor Frederick II wrote “De arte venandi cum avibus” (“On the art of hunting with birds”): he described birds from his own observation rather than from tradition, which is why the work is still regarded as one of the most accurate pre-modern books on birds.
Aus dieser Zeit stammt die Falknersprach: The language of falconry that lives on in German dates from this period: “sich mausern” (to moult) from the moult, “nicht viel Federlesens machen” (to make short work of something) from cleaning the bird, “abrichten” (to train) from training, and the “Kropf” (crop) as a sign of a well-fed falconry bird.

Feuerwaffen und Flurbereinigung verdräng: Firearms and land consolidation push hawking aside.
Ab dem 17. Jahrhundert verlor die Beizja: From the 17th century onwards hawking lost its standing. Better firearms made hunting with birds unnecessary as a source of food, and land consolidation took open space away from falcons: hedges, fences and more intensively farmed fields no longer allowed long hunting flights.
Mit dem Ende der adeligen Jagdprivilegie: With the end of the nobility's hunting privileges after 1789, falconry almost completely disappeared in Central Europe. Only a few associations, for example in the Netherlands and Great Britain, kept the knowledge alive in the 19th century.
Verbände, Zucht und Artenschutz holen di: Associations, breeding and conservation bring falconry back.
Im 20. Jahrhundert kehrte die Falknerei: In the 20th century falconry returned as a regulated form of hunting; in Germany the Deutscher Falkenorden was founded in 1923. When the Peregrine Falcon almost disappeared in the 1960s because of the insecticide DDT, falconers helped bring it back through captive breeding and release.
Seit dem Washingtoner Artenschutzabkomme: Since the 1975 Washington Convention, CITES, trade in birds of prey has been strictly regulated. Falconry birds today come from captive breeding rather than the wild, and hawking requires a hunting licence and a falconry examination.
Die UNESCO erkennt die Falknerei als leb: UNESCO recognises falconry as a living heritage.
Seit 2010 steht die Falknerei auf der Re: Since 2010 falconry has been on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, inscribed as a joint nomination by several countries from Arabia to Europe. Germany has been part of it since 2016; today more than twenty states share the inscription.
Zugleich hat die Falknerei neue Aufgaben: At the same time falconry has taken on new tasks: at airports, Eurasian Goshawks and Harris's Hawks drive birds away from runways and help prevent bird strikes. In this way the old art bridges history and nature conservation.
Auf der Arabischen Halbinsel ist die Fal: On the Arabian Peninsula falconry is closely tied to the history of the Bedouin. Saker and Peregrine Falcons in particular shape this tradition. Knowledge of birds, prey and landscape is passed down through generations.
Einordnung des Lanners: Auch er wird als: Where the Lanner fits in: it is also used as a falconry bird, but it is not the characteristic signature species of Arab falconry. The focus here is therefore on the Saker and Peregrine Falcons.
Die europäische Falknerei umfasst unters: European falconry comprises different regional traditions. In Germany the Eurasian Goshawk and the Peregrine Falcon are among the classic falconry birds: the goshawk for agile pursuit flights, the Peregrine for hunting in open airspace.
Heute werden auch amerikanische Arten wi: Today American species such as Harris's Hawk are also used. Falconry traditions are alive and not limited to the native bird species of a region.
Die nordamerikanische Falknerei machte W: North American falconry made Harris's Hawk and the Red-tailed Hawk known as falconry birds internationally. The social Harris's Hawk, often called the Harris Hawk, in particular is now found in falconry far beyond the Americas.
Der Kartenpunkt steht für die nordamerik: The map point represents the history of North American falconry. The natural range of Harris's Hawk extends from the south-western USA to South America.
Takagari heißt die japanische Kunst der: Takagari is the Japanese art of hawking. Alongside imperial court culture, samurai and shōguns shaped its history. The goshawk was a particularly prized hunting companion; valuable birds were also presented as political gifts.
Unter den Tokugawa-Shōgunen war Falknere: Under the Tokugawa shōguns falconry was more than hunting: hunting rights, hunting grounds and the gifting of birds of prey made social rank and power visible.

Persien zählt zu den großen historischen: Persia is one of the great historical heartlands of falconry. Persian treatises collected knowledge about keeping, training and caring for the birds. The Mughal rulers of India were also keen falconers: Emperor Akbar particularly valued the Eurasian Sparrowhawk.
Falknerei verband Jagdkunst mit höfische: Falconry combined the art of hunting with courtly prestige. A single place of origin for early falconry cannot be determined with certainty; Persian and Indian history form separate but connected chapters.

Berkutchi, die Adlerjäger Zentralasiens,: Berkutchi, the eagle hunters of Central Asia, hunt with Golden Eagles. In Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan this knowledge is part of regional hunting culture. In the western Mongolian province of Bayan-Ölgii, Kazakh families preserve the same tradition and pass it on within the family.
Das kirgisische Salbuurun verbindet die: The Kyrgyz salbuurun combines hunting with birds of prey with the work of taigans, a native sighthound breed. Differences between the regions lie in landscape, local transmission and the link with other forms of hunting, not in the origin of the tradition.

Ein Greifvogel auf der Faust konnte gese: A bird of prey on the fist could embody social rank. The Boke of St Albans, printed in 1486, contains a famous hierarchy that assigns particular falconry birds to different ranks of society. Falconry thus becomes a mirror of a hierarchical society.

Gerfalken aus dem hohen Norden waren an: Gyrfalcons from the far north were coveted at European and Arab courts. Particularly pale birds were considered treasures. From Iceland they reached their recipients along long trade routes and also served rulers as diplomatic gifts.
Der Handel verband Island eng mit Skandi: The trade tied Iceland closely to Scandinavia: Danish kings controlled the capture and export; later a dedicated falcon ship brought the birds to Copenhagen. The map marks Iceland as the region of origin of this historical network.
